note: City of Zumbro Falls park campground on the west bank of the Zumbro River just south of town off US 63; open grassy sites with electricity, picnic shelter, canoe/tube rental, playground. $25 a night per the city page (last updated 2022). --Claude
summary: City page read (last modified 2022): FCFS only, no reservations, ~35 sites with electricity/water, $25 a night, holiday weekends a 3-night minimum charge. Rate is 2022 so fees not written. Stored pin is on the town ballfield ~570 m north; the campground is south of the US 63 bridge (move). Possible riverfront for the river-edge tables (no site map). Google 4.2/54.
flags: PIN MOVE (~570 m): stored 44.28210,-92.42384 sits on the ballfield of the town park north of the river bridge (no campsites there on imagery). The campground, where Google pins 'Sportsman's Park Camping' (44.27648,-92.42471), is the grassy loop with tables and fire rings on the west bank of the Zumbro River south of the US 63 bridge -> move to about 44.2770,-92.4245.

Fees not written: the city page's '$25 per camper or unit, per night' was last modified 2022-07-05 (WordPress API), older than the 2024 rule. The note keeps $25 with that date. 'Camping during the Spring Creek Motocross Pro-National Event will cost $20 per person, per night.'
Standing minimum: only holiday weekends ('Holiday weekends require a 3 day minimum charge $75.00'), recorded in booking.min_stay; not an all-season minimum.

WATERFRONT (possible upgrade, unconfirmed): stored `not waterfront`. On z19 imagery a row of tables/fire rings runs along the east edge of the camping lawn, about 10-20 m from the river over open grass and a narrow reedy bank, with no road between (e.g. around 44.27768,-92.42399 and 44.27697,-92.42423). The Zumbro here measures roughly 35-45 m wide (riverfront scale). But the city posts no site map or site numbers, and imagery cannot show which tables are electric/water RV sites rather than tent spots, so no site can be named. A reviewer with a site map could upgrade to `riverfront` with a caveat; left as is here.

Pads: the sites look like open grass with tables, no gravel pads visible on imagery (padless camping: keep with a caveat, per AWH 2026-11-09). The low floodplain setting is also why the city site carries a 'Flood Information' page.
OHV/motocross: the city prices camping during the nearby Spring Creek Motocross Pro-National, but the park is a general city campground, not a staging or trail base. No action.
Phone 507-753-2568 (city page and Google) confirmed. Website confirmed (the city page; address given there is 37088 County Road 3, while Google lists 61772 US-63).
Unread: no other city page on camping exists (WordPress search for 'camp' returns only this page).
